policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'to eat their own dung', with no note attached to this unit. Qere צוֹאָתָם and ketiv חריהם both denote excrement and are both rendered 'dung' in English, so the ASV wording does not distinguish them; no italicized supply bears on the choice. Underdetermined, base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV renders 'to drink their own water', reproducing the qere euphemism מימֵי רַגְלֵיהֶם ('the water of their feet'): the noun 'water' answers to מימי, which stands only in the qere. The ketiv שיניהם is a single word for urine and yields no 'water' in English (rendered 'piss' where followed). The ASV's wording therefore distinguishes the qere.
